question: The most of the texture can be drawn with the help of drawing pen with line thickness
explanation: Standard line weights used for hatching textures and detailing correspond to option (c) per the key[cite: 1].

question: Presentation drawing are generally rendered due to
explanation: Rendering adds colors, shades, and textures to presentation drawings to give a realistic visual effect of the proposed project[cite: 1].

question: The most suitable angle for the cone of the vision for perspective drawing is
explanation: A normal comfortable human field or cone of vision for accurate, undistorted perspective drafting is typically kept within optimal limits such as 30 degrees[cite: 1].

question: The best drawing paper used for water colour is:

options.a: hand made paper (hand made drawing sheet)

explanation: Handmade or specialized heavy watercolor paper handles wet media best, though the key points to option (b)[cite: 1].

question: The length of the rectangle representing the development of the lateral surface of a right circular cylinder is equal to:

options.b: twice the circumference of circular base

explanation: When the lateral surface of a cylinder is unrolled into a flat rectangle, its width/length equals the perimeter (circumference) of its circular base[cite: 1].

question: Third angle projection is the traditional system.
explanation: Third-angle orthographic projection is widely adopted as the traditional standard system in the United States[cite: 1].

question: Engineers prefer to make ....... sketches than to pictorial sketches to clear the shape of an object.
explanation: Orthographic multi-view sketches are preferred by engineers for clarity of precise dimensions and shapes over single pictorial sketches[cite: 1].

question: The selection of suitable scale and allotment of proper space for margin, title block, revision panel, folding marks, etc. on the drawing sheet is known as:
explanation: Sheet layout involves arranging borders, title blocks, notes, and projection spaces systematically on a drawing sheet[cite: 1].

question: The size of the title block of all sizes of drawing sheet is:
explanation: Standard engineering drawing practice (e.g., BIS/ISO standards) commonly prescribes a title block size of 185 mm x 65 mm[cite: 1].

question: The projection in which the length, breadth and height of an object is shown in one view Known as:
explanation: Isometric projection is a form of pictorial projection where length, breadth, and height are all depicted simultaneously in a single view[cite: 1].

question: The shades and shadows are:

options.c: the result of object on the ground
options.d: the result of light on the ground

explanation: Shades refer to the dark areas on the object itself where light is blocked, while shadows are cast by the object onto adjacent surfaces or the ground; hence they are different[cite: 1].

question: Pencil drawings are generally corrected or revised with the help of:
explanation: An eraser shield protects surrounding lines while clean corrections are made to pencil drawings using an eraser[cite: 1].

question: Dimension lines and projection lines are drawn as

options.b: continuous thin line with zig zags

explanation: Dimension lines, extension (projection) lines, and hatching lines are standardly drawn as continuous thin lines[cite: 1].

question: Select the incorrect statement about orthographic projections:

options.a: the reference planes are also called the principle planes
options.b: the object must the situated in the first quadrant
options.c: the planes of projection and assumed to be transparent
options.d: projections are obtained by drawing perpendiculars from the object to the planes

explanation: Objects do not have to be exclusively in the first quadrant (they can be in any of the four quadrants), making option (b) or the restriction false; per the key, option (c) is listed as the selected choice[cite: 1].

question: In the first angle method of orthographic projection

options.a: the object comes between the observer and the plane
options.b: the plane comes between the object and the observer
options.c: the observer comes between the object and the plane

explanation: In first-angle projection, the observer is positioned in front of the object, and the object is situated between the observer and the projection plane[cite: 1].

question: Which of the following regarding scales in drawing is NOT true?

options.a: the name of the scale (e.g. scale 1:10) should be mentioned below the scale
options.b: a diagonal scale consists of a primary scale and a vernier
options.c: comparative scales may be plain or diagonal
options.d: when an unusual scale is used it is constructed on the drawing sheet

explanation: Diagonal scales use small subdivisions via diagonal lines, whereas vernier scales use auxiliary sliding scales; thus statement (b) regarding diagonal scales consisting of a vernier is incorrect[cite: 1].

question: The free hand drawing of an ordinary room is generally:
explanation: Interior views of an ordinary room are most commonly sketched using a two-point perspective view to show two visible walls and corners naturally[cite: 1].

question: Site plan is a type of drawing:
explanation: A site plan is a broad architectural/civil layout drawing showing property boundaries, building footprints, and surrounding layout infrastructure[cite: 1].

question: Working drawings include:

options.a: must provide complete information to produce the object
options.c: should be supplemented by further details

explanation: Working drawings must be completely self-contained and accurate, providing all necessary dimensions, notes, and details to manufacture or build the object without ambiguity[cite: 1].

question: In general structural drawings would typically include following information:
explanation: Comprehensive structural and engineering drawings incorporate orientation (north point), multi-view plans, sections, elevations, and material specifications[cite: 1].

question: A technical drawing of an object that shows the relationship or order of assembly of the various parts is known as
explanation: An exploded view drawing displays the components of an object slightly separated or stretched apart to show their assembly relationship and relative order[cite: 1].

question: The space covered by a drawing in a paper after changing the scale from 1:100 to 1:50 will:
explanation: Numerical solution: Changing the scale from 1:100 to 1:50 doubles linear dimensions ($50/100 = 0.5$, meaning scale factor doubles object size on paper by 2x). Since area scales with the square of the linear scale factor ($2^2 = 4$), the area occupied by the drawing increases by 400% (or becomes 4 times larger).
